name: xyz.proofofstock/proof-of-stock
title: Proof of Stock
description: Is this tokenized stock the issuer's own? Checks Base and Robinhood Chain, flags look-alikes.

tools.name: find_stock_token
tools.description: Find issuer-listed tokenized stocks on a chain by ticker, company name or ISIN. Returns the official contract addresses. Use it when you have a name and need the address; to check an address you already hold, use stock_passport instead, and for the whole registry list_stock_tokens. An empty result says only that the issuer lists no such token, nothing about impostors. Two chains: base (Coinbase's tokens, symbols end in "c", e.g. NVDAc) and robinhood (Robinhood's, e.g. NVDA). When the user names no chain, call it for both. Facts with their time and source, not advice: https://proofofstock.xyz/docs/legal.md

chain.description: which chain and issuer list to check: base (Coinbase's list) or robinhood (Robinhood Chain, Robinhood's list)

query.description: a ticker (NVDA or NVDAc), a company name (Tesla) or an ISIN (US67066G1040)

tools.name: list_stock_tokens
tools.description: List every token in a chain's issuer registry: symbol, name, contract address, ISIN, multiplier, whether it is minted on the chain and whether the issuer publishes a reference price. The answer opens with the exact count (also the `count` field); quote that number, do not estimate it from the list. On Base many listed tokens are not minted yet and do not trade (`minted`). Use it to enumerate or count the registry; to look up one token by name use find_stock_token, and to check one address use stock_passport. Two chains: base (Coinbase's tokens, symbols end in "c", e.g. NVDAc) and robinhood (Robinhood's, e.g. NVDA). When the user names no chain, call it for both. Facts with their time and source, not advice: https://proofofstock.xyz/docs/legal.md

chain.description: which chain and issuer list to check: base (Coinbase's list) or robinhood (Robinhood Chain, Robinhood's list)

tools.name: stock_passport
tools.description: Check one token contract address in depth. Use it when you hold one address and want the whole picture; to get the official address from a ticker or company name use find_stock_token first. It answers whether the address is in the issuer registry (and, if not, which listed stock its name imitates), the issuer reference price and its age, the latest on-chain price and its premium over that reference, the premium history split by US market session, and every gap named. Readings are recorded every 15 minutes (latest.cadence_s), so "latest" is a recorded reading, not a live quote: see latest.age_s. premium compares the latest on-chain price with the issuer reference, whose own age is reference.age_s; when the two are far apart in time, latest.premium_at_reference_time gives the premium of one moment. sources names every source and the pool rule. Every answer opens with one plain sentence; quote it. In the JSON, premium and spread are FRACTIONS (0.01 = 1%; premium > 0 means the on-chain price is above the issuer's), *_age_s and age_s are seconds before generated_at, prices are USD per token. A token is worth `multiplier` shares, and the issuer's reference is already per token. reference.kind: nav_total_return = Coinbase's NAV, token_bid_ask_mid = the mid of Robinhood's token bid/ask. notes are codes for every gap (e.g. reading_stale = our last reading is over 30 min old, pools_capped = the pool count is a minimum). Two chains: base (Coinbase's tokens, symbols end in "c", e.g. NVDAc) and robinhood (Robinhood's, e.g. NVDA). When the user names no chain, call it for both. Facts with their time and source, not advice: https://proofofstock.xyz/docs/legal.md

tools.name: verify_stock_tokens
tools.description: Before buying a token that claims to be a stock, check its contract address: is it on the issuer's own registry for this chain (Base: Coinbase; robinhood: Robinhood)? Up to 50 addresses per call. listed=true is decided by the exact address alone. listed=false means "not in this issuer's registry", not "fake" (it may be another issuer's token); impostor is set only when the token copies a listed symbol or the issuer's naming, and then listed_address is the real one. If the registry cannot be read the call fails rather than answering false. Use it when you already hold addresses; to get the official address from a ticker or company name use find_stock_token, and for one address in depth (prices, premium, its case) stock_passport. An address of the wrong form refuses the whole call before any is checked. Costs one unit of the rate limit per ten addresses. Facts, not advice.

addresses.description: the token contract addresses to check, 1 to 50, each 0x and 40 hex digits

tools.name: recent_impostors
tools.description: Tokens on a chain FIRST FLAGGED IN THE LAST 7 DAYS whose symbol or name copies an issuer-listed stock token while their contract is not in that registry, newest first (at most 50), optionally since an ISO time within that window. This is a window, not the whole list: the answer carries `window_days`, `count` for the window and `listed_total` for every look-alike on the list. Each names what it imitates and the listed address. The window is deliberate: the archive answers questions and is not a bulk download. Any one address gets its whole case at any age from verify_stock_tokens or stock_passport, and the full archive is available on request (hello@proofofstock.xyz). A claim with evidence, not a verdict.

chain.description: which chain and issuer list to check: base (Coinbase's list) or robinhood (Robinhood Chain, Robinhood's list)

since.description: only look-alikes first flagged at or after this ISO 8601 time, e.g. 2026-11-12T00:00:00Z; omit for the newest 50

tools.name: compare_venues
tools.description: Compare one share across the two venues that both list it. Use it when the question is Base against Robinhood Chain; for the largest gaps on one chain use largest_gaps, and for one contract address stock_passport. For shares listed on BOTH Base (Coinbase) and Robinhood Chain (Robinhood), matched by ISIN: per venue the on-chain price's premium over that venue's own issuer reference, the reference kind and age, the deepest pool's liquidity and the multiplier, and the gap (Robinhood premium minus Base premium) when both are current. Raw prices are never compared: multipliers and references differ (Coinbase NAV vs Robinhood bid/ask), so a gap is not a price difference or an arbitrage. Name a share by isin or by ticker (NVDA, or NVDAc); with neither, the 20 rows with the largest gap. A missing premium carries its reason; a reading older than 30 min is flagged stale and gets no gap. Facts, not advice.

isin.description: the share's ISIN, e.g. US67066G1040 for NVIDIA

symbol.description: the ticker, plain or as the issuer writes it (NVDA or NVDAc); give isin or symbol, or neither for the 20 largest gaps

tools.name: verify_anchor
tools.description: Check that our record of one UTC day has not been changed since. Omit day for the newest anchored day; a day with no anchor is an error that says so, never a guess. Every answer lists all anchored days in `days`, newest first, so another day can be asked for without guessing. Use it to audit the archive behind every verdict and behind address_on_date; it says nothing about any one token. The answer gives the SHA-256 of that day's manifest of data files, the state of its OpenTimestamps proof (pending, or the Bitcoin block it is in), the transactions carrying the same hash on Base and on Robinhood Chain, and the manifest URL and proof files: everything needed to check it WITHOUT us. Bitcoin is the root, because Base is sequenced by Coinbase and Robinhood Chain by Robinhood, the two issuers we check; the other two are mirrors, for reach.

day.description: the UTC day to check, e.g. 2026-11-12; omit for the newest anchored day

tools.name: largest_gaps
tools.description: Rank, right now, the issuer-listed tokens whose on-chain price sits furthest from the issuer's own reference price (the premium), largest first, at most 12 per chain: the same board as the site's /api/overview. Use it to see where prices diverge across a whole list; for one token use stock_passport, for one share on Base against Robinhood Chain compare_venues, and to check how current the data is data_freshness. Each row carries the premium, the deepest pool's price and liquidity, the reference price, when the on-chain price was read and how old the reference is. A reading older than 30 min is left out of the ranking and counted per chain as `stale`. A premium is a fact about two prices with their times, not a trade signal or advice.

chain.description: which chain and issuer list: base (Coinbase's list) or robinhood (Robinhood Chain, Robinhood's list); omit for both

tools.name: data_freshness
tools.description: Check how fresh this service's data is, per chain: when the issuer list was last read, when the newest on-chain pool price was recorded, when the look-alike list was rebuilt, each with its age and a state (ok, late or down) judged against the cadence that part keeps. Use it before trusting an answer that seems old, or when largest_gaps leaves rows out as stale; it answers about the service, not about any token. The same facts as the site's /status page. Takes no argument.

tools.name: address_on_date
tools.description: What a contract address was on a past UTC day, from the archive recorded at the time, never from today's state: whether it was on the issuer's list in force that day (named by the list's hash, with the URL of that exact list), whether it was an open look-alike case and what it imitated, and that day's anchor. If nothing was recorded for that day the answer says UNKNOWN; it never guesses. One address, one day per call, deliberately: the archive answers questions and is not a bulk download (the full archive is available on request, hello@proofofstock.xyz). The days that are anchored are listed by verify_anchor. Facts with their time and source, not advice.
